ownership.learnerSafeStructureOwner: Implementation owner of branch fm/pep-course-ending-html-css-js (authoring agent, not an independent critic): Course Review module and pages, this value-free coverage map and the blueprint objective list
ownership.protectedItemAuthoring: Not started. Graded item stems, options, keyed responses and feedback are authored only through a private-authoring route the course owner approves; that decision is open for this course, so no protected value exists anywhere in this task.

boundary: This file holds the planned item identifiers and format plus course-level aggregate coverage: the demand totals, the objectives the final elicits together (objectivesElicited, with per-module totals), the taught topics reached and the objectives it does not elicit. Under Firstmate decisions 009, 010 and 011 (2026-11-13), no committed file records, or lets a reader reconstruct or narrow, which module, topic or objective an item keys, which objective a distractor isolates, an item's depth, band, demand, context, notes or review findings, or per-module item counts. Those live only on the locked private question-bank and review route. This file holds no item text, options, keyed responses, feedback, scoring, rubrics or solutions.
difficultyRule: Every item is a step up from topic practice: it puts taught objectives into a new applied, debugging, browser-behaviour or accessibility context that no topic artifact.gift question, module mastery-check item, learner page activity or Course Review activity uses, and it must not reuse, lightly reword or merely combine those questions. The practice each item was compared with is recorded per item on the private route. Items need nothing outside the listed objectives as taught on the published learner pages.
elicitationRule: An objective counts as elicited by an item only when the keyed decision or one of the three distractors (one objective per distractor) depends on it alone. Each item elicits 2 to 4 objectives. The per-item objective lists stay on the private route; publicly, objectivesElicited lists the 76 objectives the items elicit together, which equal the blueprint's objective list, with per-module totals in summary.objectivesElicitedPerModule. The private owner check on 2026-11-13 confirmed that the union of the private per-item lists equals this list, that each item lists 2 to 4 objectives and that no two items share a keyed objective.
itemConstraints: Each item asks for exactly one keyed decision on at most one short listing.
Each item stays within its private reading budget: stem words, lines of code or markup (never more than 6) and total option words.
Each item uses only syntax, APIs and behaviour taught on the published learner pages of its topics; grep the learner artifact.html files for every API an item uses before keying it.
Each item's context differs from every practice item it was compared with on the private route and steps up from it.

Every option's stated outcome is confirmed in a current Chromium or Node.js 24 run (server responses stubbed with already-settled promises or a local server), or against the cited official source where it cannot run offline, before keying.
Each item's depth follows the policy recorded on the private route.

No trick questions: no key turns on an unusual reading of the stem, a typo or near-identical spelling, a double negative, an 'all/none of the above' option, or browser-version trivia; every distractor is a plausible error a learner makes on the objective that distractor isolates.

No busywork or padding: no two items share a keyed objective (checked on the private route) or a context type, no item exists only to raise a module's count, and every item asks for an implementation, debugging or tracing decision a web developer actually makes.
Named exceptions to the taught-syntax rule are recorded and checked per item on the private route.

Leak test (loops 5 to 8, decisions 009 to 011): no committed field, aggregate, ordering or derived value may let a reader rule an option in or out, confirm a key, or narrow the module, topic or objective an item keys. Per-item contexts, demand labels, notes and review findings stay on the private route.
progressionRule: Items are delivered in id order, easier to harder. How difficulty is assigned, and the check that the order follows it, are recorded on the private route. Real difficulty is confirmed by pilot data on the private authoring route.
formativeQuizRule: Topic artifact.gift practice quizzes are separate from this graded MCQ: each is a quick formative verification capped at five minutes. A quiz need not fill the cap, and no fixed per-question duration is assumed for it. This supersedes the intake's 'about 30 seconds per question' planning note for the Concept-day Mini-quiz block.
readingEstimateRule: Per-item reading budgets are kept on the private route, and only the planned total and maximum are published. readingEstimateSeconds = (stemWordsMax + optionWordsMax) / 230 words per minute + 4 seconds per code line + decisionSeconds (8 by default, more for items whose options each need a calculation). The planned total must stay at or under 90% of the 30-minute sitting; pilot timing of the real item text happens on the private authoring route, because it cannot be done value-free.

timing.rule: Firstmate instruction 005 (2026-11-12, updated captain intent): exactly 30 questions. The single course MCQ identity and its accepted 30-minute duration are kept (Firstmate decision hcj-base, 2026-11-09, which also keeps the Foundation-final 2-minutes-per-question rule off this Standard/Fast course). No per-question timer.
timing.envelope: Unchanged 30-minute MCQ slot of the course timing envelope (shared final target 90-minute practical + 30-minute MCQ on Standard and Fast).

separatePractical.note: Unchanged and not part of this record.

baseline.canonicalBreakdown: 25 core + 1 Reading from S20-S26, plus the 3 S27 Project-day core topics; part of the 243-topic canonical baseline

objectivesNotElicited.reason: Hands-on production objectives performed in real tools are not assessed by multiple choice. Scaffolding a Vite project (project-setup-with-npm-and-vite o1) is evidenced by the S27 project and the graded practical. Setting breakpoints and finding the faulty line in real DevTools (debugging-with-devtools-breakpoints o1, o3) are evidenced by the debugging page's practice script and its module mastery check; no lab.json or graded blueprint lists them. Writing a closure that keeps private state (scope-and-closures o2) is an objective of the javascript-fundamentals module lab and of the graded practical web-client-practical. Writing and running Vitest tests (testing-a-plain-function-with-vitest o1, o2) are objectives of the fetch-and-browser-client module lab and of the graded practical web-client-practical. The viewport-meta explanation (responsive-mobile-first-layout o2) left the graded MCQ with the 30-item reduction; it stays in the html-and-css module lab, its topic's page activity and its practice quiz.
